'''Albrecht Bertram''' (* October 2, 1950, in [[Braunschweig]]) is a former university professor of mechanics. He held the Chair of Strength of Materials of the Institute of Mechanics (IFME) at the [[Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg]] and is an associate professor at the Department of [[Continuum Mechanics]] and Material Theory of the Institute of Mechanics at [[Technische Universität Berlin]].

== Life and career ==
During his career he had several guest stays at the following universities:<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bertram |first1=Albrecht |title=Website of Albrecht Bertram at TU Berlin |url=https://www.lkm.tu-berlin.de/menue/mitarbeiterinnen_sprechstunden/prof_dr_ing_a_bertram/ |website=www.lkm.tu-berlin.de/menue/mitarbeiterinnen_sprechstunden/prof_dr_ing_a_bertram/ |publisher=TU Berlin |accessdate=September 28, 2019}}</ref>
* [[Universidad Industrial de Santander]], Bucaramanga, Columbia, 1983 to 1985 (lecturer)
* [[University of Dar es Salaam]], Tansania, 1986 (guest lecturer)
* [[Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro]], Brasilia, 1987 (research stay)
* [[Ecole des Mines]] in Paris, Frankreich, 2005 (guest professor)
* [[University of Havana]], Cuba, 2010 guest professor)
* [[University of California, Berkeley|University of California at Berkeley]], USA, 2010 (guest scientist)

== Research focus ==
Bertram's work focuses on material modelling. The background is the continuum thermomechanically consistent development of extended approaches for engineering applications.<ref>{{cite web|title=IFME {{!}} LTM {{!}} Albrecht Bertram|periodical=|publisher=|url=http://www.ifme.ovgu.de/bertram-karte-698.html|url-status=dead|accessdate=January 29, 2017|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170129123613/http://www.ifme.ovgu.de/bertram-karte-698.html|archivedate=January 29, 2017|last=|date=|year=|language=|pages=|quote=}}</ref> The work covers the entire range of inelastic material behaviour with geometric non-linearity.

In addition, he deals with the basics of generalized continuum theories, especially the continua where higher gradients of the displacements are used.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Bertram |first1=Albrecht |title=Compendium on Gradient Materials |date=June 2019 |location=Berlin |pages=237 |edition=3rd |doi=10.13140/RG.2.2.36769.51045 }}</ref>

== Miscellaneous ==
Bertram is considered as a representative of the so-called 'Berlin School of Continuum Mechanics'.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Bertram |first1=Albrecht |title=Elasticity and Plasticity of Large Deformation |date=2012 |publisher=Springer |location=Berlin Heidelberg |isbn=978-3-642-24614-2 |edition=3rd |url=https://www.springer.com/de/book/9783642246142 |accessdate=September 28, 2019}}</ref> This school is strongly influenced by works of the scientists [[Clifford Truesdell]] and [[Walter Noll]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Truesdell |first1=Clifford |title=The Non-Linear Field Theories of Mechanics |date=1992 |publisher=Springer |location=Berlin Heidelberg |isbn=978-3-662-13183-1 |pages=591 |edition=3rd |url=https://www.springer.com/de/book/9783662131831 |accessdate=September 28, 2019}}</ref> He is known for his precise representations based on mathematical and physical principles while avoiding purely intuitive approaches.
